note: City of Winfield fairgrounds on US-160 at 1105 W. Ninth, by the Walnut River, open for camping year-round outside events too. Open camping areas with about 150 50-amp services on hard surface plus 20/30-amp outlets, limited seasonal water, a year-round dump station; the 44-acre Pecan Grove to the south has limited electric. Restrooms close in winter. After 14 days, move between the fairgrounds and the Pecan Grove. --Claude
summary: City page + Jan 2026 fee schedule: $17 per 24 h confirmed; electric 50 and water confirmed, sewer true -> cleared (no sewer hookups, dump only); max_rig_ft 50 -> cleared (unsourced; permit covers a 40x20 ft spot); dump, year-round, FCFS confirmed. Not waterfront stands. No split (Pecan Grove ~580 m S). Year-round daily camping for anyone, so not event-only.
flags: NOT EVENT-ONLY: 'Daily Camping (24 hr) Campsites are available year-round. Single units and groups are welcome.' Campers in 8/2025, 5/2022 and 9/2019 stayed on ordinary nights. Some areas can be crowded or closed during the fair or the Walnut Valley Festival, though I couldn't read a closure calendar.

SPLIT: not a candidate. The Pecan Grove (44 acres, 'limited electrical and (seasonal) water hookups') is the wooded river bend about 580 m S of the pin (near 37.2333,-97.0120). That's under 1 km, it's reached by the fairgrounds' own internal road, and the city treats the two as one camping system with one permit, one fee and a 14-day rule that moves you between them.

WATERFRONT 'not waterfront' stands, though the river view is uncertain. The pinned loop's west road sits 50-70 m from the Walnut River behind a solid tree belt. In the Pecan Grove a lane runs along the bank with a thin tree fringe, so riverbank spots may exist, but they're under canopy and imagery can't confirm them. The only support is the city's marketing line 'Camp along the banks of the Walnut River', which can't earn an upgrade. Possible riverview lead for the Pecan Grove only.
PIN 37.2385,-97.01126 is in the tree-shaded camping loops just W of the exhibit buildings. OK.
PHONE 620-221-5520 confirmed (City Public Improvements Department, on the fairgrounds page). WEBSITE fine.

SEWER cleared: the old note's 'full-hookup' isn't on the city page, which lists electric, limited seasonal water and a dump station, and no camper reported sewer. The 2022 camper found flooding had closed spaces (river floodplain).
UNREAD: the ePermits camping-permit page (script-only), so I don't know whether the permit must be bought online or can still be paid at the 'courtesy box' a 2019 camper used.
